editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher article text, critic review text, plot synopses, parents-guide text and aggregator blurbs are never copied; Swoon'd writes its own explanation and links to the original. No posters, key art, stills, trailers, clips, score audio, film sound effects or dialogue are displayed or hosted.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: I can follow and join a conversation about horror films, whatever my own scare tolerance: I understand what people mean when they talk about how a scare is built, which kind of horror a film is, where it sits in the genre's history and fights, and how horror fans share it, and I can ask honest, curious questions and honour comfort limits without pretending to have watched everything.

licensingConstraints.constraint: No film posters, key art, stills, frame grabs, mask or monster images. All images are original abstract Swoon'd technique illustrations (license id original-swoond) and none depicts a frightening scene. Titles are text only.
No trailers or clips are embedded, hosted or re-cut; link-out to official channels only, no autoplay, and hidden at the gentle comfort level.

No film score, soundtrack, sound effects or dialogue audio. Listening exercises use original or synthesised cues only (original-swoond), loudness-capped, with skip, a text alternative and equal mastery credit.
Never copy publisher articles, critic review text, plot synopses, aggregator blurbs or parents-guide text; explain in Swoon'd words and link.

TMDB API is non-commercial only without a written agreement (attribution, no caching beyond 6 months, no AI/ML use, JustWatch credit); OMDb is CC BY-NC; IMDb datasets are non-commercial; Letterboxd API is not granted for recommendation or LLM projects. None are production dependencies before a licence. Wikidata (CC0) and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) are allowed with attribution.
Studio, distributor, label, festival and franchise logos (A24, Neon, Blumhouse, Shudder, Fangoria, Arrow, Scream Factory) are trademarks: text-only mentions.
Actor and director names appear as facts only; no likeness, endorsement or fabricated quotes. Public professional record only; no dramatisation of real victims or real cases.

Ratings figures and parents-guide or content-warning data (Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, CinemaScore, IMDb, Letterboxd, Common Sense Media, community content-warning sites) belong to their providers or users: no scraping or mirrored tables; link out or write our own one-line description with a link to the official ratings board.

safetyConstraints: Violence and gore are always described at a non-graphic level at every comfort setting; no gore or frightening imagery is ever shown.

Content comfort: a learner-controlled comfort dial (gentle, balanced, full) changes delivery only; every audio or intensity-flagged item has a text twin with equal mastery credit, can be skipped without penalty, and is never rewarded as bravery. No courage badges, dares, kill-count scoring or leaderboards.
Audio is original, loudness-normalised and capped; no sudden peaks at balanced, no infrasound, no flashing or strobe.

Sensitive topics (suicide, self-harm, child harm, sexual violence, animal harm, mental illness) appear only as topic names in content-note literacy, with a content-note line before any lesson that names one; they are skippable without loss.
Never push R-rated or unrated titles at a reader of unknown age; teach ratings literacy instead. Never suggest or link to unlicensed sources for watching films.
Films 'based on a true story' and paranormal claims are taught as marketing and folklore; real victims and real cases are not dramatised.
